2025_310_march_2025_financial_statement.paragraph: Unaudited statements of revenues and expenditures for Troy School District covering the period July 1, 2024 through March 31, 2025, presented in the May 20, 2025 board packet and covering the General Fund, the Consolidated Debt Service Funds, four special revenue funds, the Sinking Fund and two capital projects funds. General Fund actual revenues of $128,490,398 against actual expenditures of $120,509,744 produced revenues over expenditures of $7,980,654 for the nine months, against an approved budget that anticipated revenues under expenditures of $(3,489,920) for the full year.

2025_310_march_2025_financial_statement.verbose:
Troy School District's unaudited Statements of Revenues and Expenditures for the period July 1, 2024 through March 31, 2025, distributed with the May 20, 2025 Board of Education materials. Nine separate fund statements are presented, each with an Approved (budget) column and an Actual column: the General Fund, the Consolidated Debt Service Funds, Special Revenue Fund - Troy Preschool Fund (531), Special Revenue Fund - Community Service Fund (530), Special Revenue Fund - Troy Career Center Fund (529), Special Revenue Fund - Food Service Fund (520), Sinking Fund (498), 2023 Capital Projects Fund (423), and 2019 Capital Projects Fund (419).

GENERAL FUND
Revenues by source, budget then actual: Local Sources 47,121,701 and 44,806,139.77; State Sources 130,543,892 and 73,272,560.37; Federal Sources 4,459,948 and 1,348,789.70; Interdistrict Sources 12,962,074 and 9,062,908. Total Revenues are budgeted at $195,087,615 with actual of $128,490,398.

Instruction expenditures, budget then actual: Basic Programs 95,192,480 and 54,532,722; Added Needs 31,226,841 and 20,599,025; Adult Education 959,868 and 634,093; Total Instruction 127,379,189 and 75,765,841.

Support Services expenditures, budget then actual: Pupil 15,761,790 and 9,594,937; Instructional Staff 12,897,273 and 7,618,427; General Administration 2,276,464 and 1,560,476; School Administration 10,144,557 and 6,676,349; Business Services 1,719,542 and 1,196,020; Operations 15,443,900 and 10,290,198; Pupil Transportation 5,441,163 and 2,694,974; Central Services 3,961,841 and 2,963,790; Support Services (Athletics and Other) 2,701,846 and 1,792,046; Total Support Services 70,348,376 and 44,387,217.

Remaining General Fund expenditure categories: Community Services 199,687 budget and 189,533 actual; Debt Service 478,500 budget and 167,153 actual; Outgoing Transfers/Other 171,783 budget with no actual recorded. Total Expenditures are budgeted at $198,577,535 with actual of $120,509,744. Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures is $(3,489,920) on the approved budget and $7,980,654 actual.

CONSOLIDATED DEBT SERVICE FUNDS
Revenues: Local Sources 31,014,230 budget and 31,926,646 actual; State Sources 344,311 budget and 360,169 actual. Expenditures: Principal 21,415,000 budget with no actual recorded; Interest 10,292,350 budget and 5,146,265 actual; Other Transactions 2,125 budget and 1,150 actual. Total Revenues $31,358,541 budget and $32,286,816 actual; Total Expenditures $31,709,475 budget and $5,147,415 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $(350,934) budget and $27,139,401 actual. The absence of any principal payment through March 31 is the dominant reason actual expenditures remain far below the approved figure.

SPECIAL REVENUE FUND - TROY PRESCHOOL FUND (531)
Revenues: Local Sources 1,982,380 budget and 1,397,823 actual; State Sources 2,981,177 budget and 1,804,638 actual. Expenditures: Salaries 1,778,056 and 1,098,544; Employee Benefits 947,363 and 613,525; Purchased Services 1,105,902 and 635,679; Supplies and Materials 391,305 and 105,780; Capital Outlay 147,358 and 23,684; Other with no budget and 102,298 actual; Debt Service 497,665 budget with no actual. Total Revenues $4,963,557 budget and $3,202,461 actual; Total Expenditures $4,867,649 budget and $2,579,510 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $95,908 budget and $622,951 actual.

SPECIAL REVENUE FUND - COMMUNITY SERVICE FUND (530)
Revenues: Local Sources 1,827,940 budget and 1,290,143 actual, the fund's only revenue source. Expenditures: Salaries 761,694 and 515,828; Employee Benefits 379,851 and 266,229; Purchased Services 894,048 and 621,955; Supplies and Materials 55,500 and 20,815; Capital Outlay 15,000 budget with no actual; Other with neither budget nor actual. Total Revenues $1,827,940 budget and $1,290,143 actual; Total Expenditures $2,106,093 budget and $1,424,827 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $(278,153) budget and $(134,684) actual.

SPECIAL REVENUE FUND - TROY CAREER CENTER FUND (529)
Revenues: State Sources 551,146 budget and 278,656 actual; Federal Sources 2,370,111 budget and 1,563,633 actual. Expenditures: Salaries 1,069,778 and 796,835; Employee Benefits 640,451 and 481,814; Purchased Services 801,478 and 711,299; Supplies and Materials 5,550 budget and (858) actual, a credit balance; Capital Outlay 15,000 and 7,210; Other 10,000 budget and 286,743 actual; Debt Service 264,000 budget with no actual. Total Revenues $2,921,257 budget and $1,842,289 actual; Total Expenditures $2,921,257 budget and $2,283,044 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures is zero on the budget and $(440,755) actual - the only operating fund other than Community Service and Food Service running an actual deficit at this point in the year.

SPECIAL REVENUE FUND - FOOD SERVICE FUND (520)
Revenues: Local Sources 352,744 budget and 162,099 actual; State Sources 4,847,963 budget and 2,897,128 actual; Federal Sources 2,343,186 budget and 1,623,886 actual; Interdistrict Sources 1,400 budget and 700 actual. Expenditures: Salaries 82,807 and 63,698; Employee Benefits 6,335 and 4,873; Purchased Services 2,919,708 and 2,117,134; Supplies and Materials 655,000 budget and 2,210,585 actual, well above the budgeted amount; Capital Outlay 4,188,216 budget and 520,255 actual; Other 825,000 budget and 16,153 actual; Transfers Out 54,500 budget with no actual. Total Revenues $7,545,293 budget and $4,683,813 actual; Total Expenditures $8,731,566 budget and $4,932,697 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $(1,186,273) budget and $(248,884) actual.

SINKING FUND (498)
Revenues: Local Sources 5,090,000 budget and 5,009,393 actual. Expenditures: Capital Outlay 4,656,984 budget and 3,522,861 actual. Total Revenue $5,090,000 budget and $5,009,393 actual; Total Expenditures $4,656,984 budget and $3,522,861 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $433,016 budget and $1,486,532 actual. Sinking fund levy collections are essentially complete for the year while capital outlay continues.

2023 CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND (423)
Revenues: Local Sources 6,000,000 budget and 5,932,749 actual. Expenditures: Purchased Services with no budget and 452,906 actual; Capital Outlay 75,000,000 budget and 31,481,600 actual; Outgoing Transfers 12,600,000 budget and 216,330 actual. Total Revenue $6,000,000 budget and $5,932,749 actual; Total Expenditures $87,600,000 budget and $32,150,837 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $(81,600,000) budget and $(26,218,088) actual. This is the district's active bond construction fund, spending bond proceeds held from the 2023 authorization, so a large excess of expenditures over current-year revenues is expected.

2019 CAPITAL PROJECTS FUND (419)
Revenues: Local Sources 50,000 budget and 40,727 actual, essentially investment earnings on remaining proceeds. Expenditures: Capital Outlay 1,109,463 budget and 30,845 actual; Support Services - Central with neither budget nor actual amounts. Total Revenue $50,000 budget and $40,727 actual; Total Expenditures $1,109,463 budget and $30,845 actual; Revenues Over (Under) Expenditures $(1,059,463) budget and $9,882 actual. The 2019 program is nearly wound down, with only minimal spending recorded in the current year.

All statements are labeled unaudited and cover three quarters of the 2024-25 fiscal year, so actual columns reflect nine months of collections and disbursements against full-year approved budgets. State Sources in the General Fund, debt service principal, and capital outlay in the Food Service and 2023 Capital Projects funds are the lines where the actual and approved columns diverge most visibly.

2025_311_ocsba_bylaws_amendments_at_a_gl.paragraph: Summary sheet prepared by the Oakland County School Boards Association listing the proposed 2025 amendments to its bylaws, organized as four clerical or grammatical corrections that do not change meaning followed by eight sections revised for content, each keyed to page, article and section with a rationale. The most substantive changes add a new Article VII, Section 10 requiring the Board of Directors to create and maintain Board Operating Procedures, allow the Office of Secretary to be split into Corresponding and Recording Secretary roles, and move committee chair elections from after January 31st to after July 1st to align with the July 1 - June 30 operating year.
2025_311_ocsba_bylaws_amendments_at_a_gl.page:
**Purpose**
An "Amendments at a Glance" companion to the redlined OCSBA bylaws, identifying each proposed change by page, article and section and giving the committee's rationale. The changes are split into two groups: clerical/grammatical revisions that do not change meaning, and sections revised and edited for content.

**Clerical and grammatical revisions (four)**
1. Page 3, Article V, Section 3, Place of Meeting - correcting "off" to "office" where the text refers to the registered office of the Association as the default meeting place.
2. Page 6, Article VIII, Section 2, Term of Office - deleting the stray "r" so "Ther" reads "The" in the section governing officer terms, removal with cause by affirmative vote of a majority of the Directors, and the filling of vacancies.
3. Page 9, Article IX, Section 4, The Government Relations Committee - adding "on" after "information" in the description of the standing committee, which meets at least 6 times per year.
4. Page 15, Article XIV, Section 2, Dealing with the Association - removing a duplicated phrase in the conflict-of-interest provision on contracts between the Association and its directors or officers.

**Revisions for content (eight)**
1. Page 5, Article VII, Section 4, Notice - deleting language on giving special meeting notice by fax and by U.S. mail, described as outdated modes of communication; notice of a special meeting of the Board of Directors is given at least two days by written notice delivered personally, by phone, fax, or email.
2. Page 6, Article VII, Section 10, Board Operating Procedures - new section requiring the Board of Directors to create and maintain Board Operating Procedures to be used in conjunction with the bylaws, added because the Board recently adopted such procedures defining roles, responsibilities and timelines.
3. Page 7, Article VIII, Section 6, The Secretary - permitting the Board, at its discretion on an annual basis, to divide the Office of Secretary into Corresponding Secretary and Recording Secretary; rationale cites a Board of 7-9 directors and additional leadership opportunities.
4. Page 8, Article IX, Section 3, Committee Chairs - moving the chair election from the first committee meeting after January 31st to after July 1st, with written notice of the election date, time and place at least seven (7) calendar days before the vote; rationale is alignment with the July 1 - June 30 operating year.
5. Page 9, Article IX, Section 4, The Government Relations Committee - membership and leadership language providing that each Member School District appoint a representative at its annual organizational meeting, that each district in attendance has one (1) vote cast by its appointed representative, and that in the absence of an elected Vice Chair the Vice President of OCSBA assumes the position, to build leadership on GRC.
6. Page 9, Article IX, Section 5, Resolutions and Bylaws Committee - shifting appointment of committee members from the Board of Directors to the OCSBA President annually, consistent with common practice; the Government Relations Committee Chairperson is a member of the committee, which meets at least once per year.
7. Page 16, Article XV, Section 5, Method of Giving Notices - replacing mailing with electronic communication to a director's or officer's last known district-provided email address, because OCSBA does not physically mail communications.
8. Page 17, Article XVI, Section 1, Amendments - retaining amendment by vote of the Member School Districts on a written ballot with at least a forty (40) day voting period and one vote per district, while allowing the Board of Directors to correct grammatical errors that do not change meaning or intent without a vote of the membership.
2025_311_ocsba_bylaws_amendments_at_a_gl.verbose:
"OCSBA Bylaws - Amendments at a Glance" is the crosswalk document accompanying the redlined Oakland County School Boards Association bylaws presented to the Troy School District Board of Education on May 20, 2025. It sorts the proposed 2025 amendments into two categories and gives, for each, the page number in the bylaws, the article and section affected, the operative language, and a rationale.

CLERICAL AND GRAMMATICAL REVISIONS
The document states that four revisions are clerical or grammatical in nature and do not change the meaning of the bylaws.

First, Page 3, Article V, Section 3, Place of Meeting. The Board of Directors may designate the place of meeting for any annual or regular meeting or for any special meeting; if no designation is made, or if a special meeting is otherwise called, the place of the meeting will be the registered office of the Association; but if all of the Members meet at any time and place and consent to holding of a meeting, such meeting will be valid without call or notice, and at such meeting any corporate action may be taken. Rationale: grammar and clarification, since "off" is supposed to be "office."

Second, Page 6, Article VIII, Section 2, Term of Office. The term of office for all officers commences upon their election or appointment and continues until the next annual meeting of the Association and thereafter until their respective successors are chosen or until their resignation or removal. Any officer may be removed from office at any meeting of the Directors, with cause, by the affirmative vote of a majority of the Directors, whenever in their judgment the best interests of the Association will be served thereby. An officer may resign by written notice to the Association, effective upon receipt or at a subsequent time specified in the notice. The Directors have power to fill any vacancies in any offices occurring for whatever reason. Rationale: grammar/clarity - deleting the "r" in the first word to change "Ther" to "The."

Third, Page 9, Article IX, Section 4, The Government Relations Committee. The Government Relations Committee shall be a standing committee whose purpose is to receive information on legislative matters for the purpose of sharing said information with the Member School Districts to advocate for, and increase awareness of, issues facing public education. The committee will meet at least 6 times per year. The correction inserts "on" after "information."

Fourth, Page 15, Article XIV, Section 2, Dealing with the Association. The provision states that a contract or other transaction between the Association and one or more of its directors or officers, or between the Association and a domestic or foreign corporation, firm or association of any type or kind in which one or more of the Association's directors or officers are trustees or officers, or are otherwise interested, is not void or voidable solely because of such common trusteeship, officership or interest, or solely because such directors are present at the meeting of the Board of Directors or committee thereof at which such contract or transaction is acted upon, or solely because their votes are counted for such purpose, if any of the stated conditions is satisfied. Rationale: to remove a duplicate phrase.

SECTIONS REVISED AND EDITED FOR CONTENT
The document then lists eight sections revised for content.

1. Page 5, Article VII, Section 4, Notice. Notice of any special meeting of the Board of Directors will be given at least two days by written notice delivered personally, by phone, fax, or email to each Director's contact information as shown by the records of the Association, or five days' notice by mail; if mailed, such notice is deemed delivered when deposited in the United States mail in a sealed envelope so addressed with postage prepaid. Any Director may waive notice; attendance at any meeting constitutes waiver except where a Director attends for the express purpose of objecting to the transaction of business because the meeting is not lawfully called or convened. Neither the business to be transacted at, nor the purpose of, any regular or special meeting need be specified in the notice or waiver unless specifically required by law or the bylaws. Rationale: deleting language that refers to sending meeting notices via U.S. mail and fax, which are outdated modes of communication.

2. Page 6, Article VII, Section 10, Board Operating Procedures. A new section reading: "The Board of Directors shall create and maintain Board Operating Procedures which shall be used in conjunction with these Bylaws." Rationale: adding this section as the Board of Directors recently adopted Board Operating Procedures that further define roles, responsibilities and timelines.

3. Page 7, Article VIII, Section 6, The Secretary. The Secretary attends all meetings of the Board of Directors and records all votes and the minutes of all proceedings in a book kept for that purpose; gives or causes to be given notice of all meetings of the Directors for which notice may be required; performs other duties as prescribed by the Directors; and has authority to execute with the President all authorized conveyances, contracts or other obligations in the name of the Association, except as otherwise directed by the Directors. The amendment adds that at the discretion of the Board of Directors on an annual basis, the Office of Secretary may be divided into two roles: Corresponding Secretary and Recording Secretary. Rationale: with a Board of 7-9 directors, it is helpful to split the role of Secretary into two and provides additional leadership opportunities.

4. Page 8, Article IX, Section 3, Committee Chairs. Each standing and ad hoc committee shall elect a Chairperson annually from the appointed representatives, with the election as the first order of business at the committee's first meeting after July 1st, replacing January 31st, unless otherwise specified in the bylaws. Written notice of the election date, time and place shall be provided to all appointed representatives not less than seven (7) calendar days prior to the meeting at which the vote will occur. Rationale: the Operating Year is July 1 - June 30 and this change brings the bylaws into alignment.

5. Page 9, Article IX, Section 4, The Government Relations Committee. Beyond the standing committee description and the at-least-6-meetings-per-year requirement, the amendment adds Committee Membership/Leadership language: at each Member School District's annual organizational meeting, a Member should be appointed to represent that district on the Government Relations Committee; a Committee Chairperson will be elected annually from the appointed Members at the first committee meeting after January 31st; each Member School District in attendance shall have one (1) vote, cast by the district's appointed representative; and in the absence of an elected Vice Chair, the Vice President of OCSBA will assume the position of Vice Chair. Rationale: to ensure the association is building leadership on GRC.

6. Page 9, Article IX, Section 5, Resolutions and Bylaws Committee. The committee is a standing committee that develops and manages the resolutions and bylaws process and meets at least once per year. Under Committee Membership/Leadership, committee members will be appointed by the OCSBA President annually rather than by the Board of Directors; members may be reappointed for additional terms; the appointed members elect a Committee Chairperson at the first committee meeting after appointment; and the Government Relations Committee Chairperson shall be a member of the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee. Rationale: common practice is that the OCSBA President makes committee appointments.

7. Page 16, Article XV, Section 5, Method of Giving Notices. Any notice required by statute or by the bylaws to be given to the directors, or to any officers of the Association unless otherwise provided, shall be given by electronic communication to such director or officer at his or her last known district-provided email address as the same appears on the records of the Association, and such notice shall be deemed to have been given at the time of such communication - replacing the prior references to mailing. Rationale: OCSBA does not physically mail communications.

8. Page 17, Article XVI, Section 1, Amendments. The bylaws may be altered or amended by the vote of the Member School Districts; the Board of Directors will provide a written ballot with the proposed amendment(s) to each Member School District giving at least a forty (40) day period in which to vote, and each Member School District will have one vote. The amendment adds that grammatical errors that do not change the meaning or intent of the language may be corrected by the Board of Directors without a vote of the membership. Rationale: small grammatical errors such as grammar and spelling that do not change meaning or intent can be corrected by the Board of Directors during the annual review rather than having to go out to the membership for a vote.

Taken together, the package modernizes notice provisions from mail and fax to email, codifies Board Operating Procedures in the bylaws, creates flexibility to split the Secretary role, realigns committee chair elections and appointment authority with the association's July-to-June operating year and the President's customary appointment power, and gives the Board limited authority to fix typographical errors without a full membership ballot.

2025_312_ocsba_bylaws_showing_changes.paragraph: Full redlined text of the Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, with the proposed 2025 amendments and their rationales shown in place, submitted for Troy School District board consideration on May 20, 2025. The document carries adoption history of Board of Directors 11/15/2017, General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018, and amendments approved by Member School Districts on 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021 and 3/3/2023, and runs from Article I offices at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, through Article XVI amendments plus Appendix 1 defining cause for removal.
2025_312_ocsba_bylaws_showing_changes.page:
**Identification and adoption history**
Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, shown with tracked changes and rationale notes. Adopted by Board of Directors 11/15/2017; adopted by General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018; amendments approved by Member School Districts 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021 and 3/3/2023.

**Articles I-V: offices, purpose, membership, dues, member meetings**
The principal office is at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland, Michigan. Purposes include advancing public education quality in Oakland County, sponsoring programs in partnership with Oakland Schools, and advocating for legislation supporting public education. Membership is open to publicly elected board members of Oakland County school districts and elected Oakland ISD board members whose districts are in good standing with MASB. Each Member has one vote; each Member School District has one vote on resolutions and bylaw amendments. Electronic voting is granted to the Board of Directors only for emergency business. Financing comes from an annual MASB grant to CASBA members, ISD dues not exceeding the MASB CASBA grant, and contributions. There is an annual meeting plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1; special meetings require 30 days' notice; written notice of meetings is delivered not less than ten nor more than fifty days before; a quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of Member School Districts.

**Articles VI-VIII: directors and officers**
The Board consists of an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9, with three-year terms and only one Member per district serving at a time. By May 1st yearly an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Directors is convened; elections occur at the June meeting; nominations cannot be made from the floor. Failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes a resignation absent an excused absence requested in writing within thirty (30) days. Special meeting notice is at least two days; a majority is a quorum. New Section 10 requires Board Operating Procedures. Officers are President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer; the Secretary role may be divided into Corresponding and Recording Secretary at the Board's annual discretion.

**Article IX: committees**
Quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives. Chairs are elected at the first meeting after July 1st (changed from January 31st) with seven (7) calendar days' written notice. The Government Relations Committee meets at least 6 times per year; the OCSBA Vice President serves as Vice Chair absent an elected one. The Resolutions and Bylaws Committee meets at least once per year, with members appointed by the OCSBA President. Member School District voting windows are at least forty (40) calendar days, and resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association.

**Articles X-XVI and Appendix 1**
Dissolution follows Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation; no inurement under Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. Board approval and signature of both President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500; expenditures up to $2,500 need either the President or Treasurer. The Treasurer presents a budget for the fiscal year (July 1 to June 30) no later than the June Board meeting and end-of-year revenue and expense reports no later than August 30th. The Board may enter an Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools. Article XII provides indemnification under the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act. Notices are given by electronic communication to district-provided email addresses. Appendix 1, adopted by the OCSBA Board of Directors on September 16, 2020, defines cause for removal by reference to the duties of care, loyalty and obedience.
2025_312_ocsba_bylaws_showing_changes.verbose:
Complete redlined text of the Bylaws of the Oakland County School Boards Association, presented with the proposed 2025 amendments and inline rationale notes. The cover block records: Adopted by Board of Directors 11/15/2017; Adopted by General Membership 1/24/2018 and 10/18/2018; Amendments Approved by Member School Districts 9/16/2020, 9/10/2021 and 3/3/2023.

ARTICLE I - OFFICES. The principal office of the Association in Michigan is at 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford Township, County of Oakland; a registered office and registered agent must be continuously maintained.

ARTICLE II - PURPOSE. Eight purposes: advancing the quality of public education in Oakland County through cooperative efforts of locally elected boards of education; promoting high standards in educational programs and services; informing school board members on educational issues; conducting and sponsoring meetings and programs in partnership with Oakland Schools; promoting public understanding of the role of school boards; enhancing cooperation among Oakland County boards; representing school board views to political representatives; and advocating for county, state and national legislation supporting public education.

ARTICLE III - MEMBERSHIP. Any publicly elected Board of Education member of an Oakland County school district, or any elected Oakland ISD Board of Education member, whose district is a member in good standing of the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB), is an eligible general member. Each Member has one vote, cast in person; by exception, each Member School District has one (1) vote on resolutions under Article IX and on bylaw amendments under Article XVI, with results provided to all Member Districts no later than the next general membership meeting. Electronic voting rights are granted to the Board of Directors only for emergency business, with all electronic votes reaffirmed at the next Board meeting. Membership is not transferable.

ARTICLE IV - DUES. The Association is financed by an annual MASB grant to its County Area School Boards Association (CASBA) members, Intermediate School District membership dues not exceeding the MASB CASBA grant, and contributions and gifts.

ARTICLE V - MEETING OF MEMBERS. An annual meeting plus not less than three additional regular membership meetings each year; the annual meeting is the first regular meeting after July 1. Special meetings may be called by voice or email by the President or by two or more Board members with 30 days’ notice. Section 3, Place of Meeting, carries the correction of "off" to "office" for the registered office default. Written notice is delivered personally or by email not less than ten nor more than fifty days before the meeting by the Secretary. Quorum is at least one Member from twenty-five (25%) percent of the Member School Districts.

ARTICLE VI - ELECTION OF BOARD OF DIRECTORS. The Board consists of an odd number of Directors, no fewer than 7 nor more than 9; a decrease is accomplished by attrition, which may result in an eight member Board for up to one year until the next election. Only one Member from each Member School District may serve at a time, and terms are three (3) years. By May 1st yearly the Board convenes an Election Committee of the three most recently elected Members of the Board of Directors, which seeks candidates providing geographical balance throughout Oakland County; Board Candidate Application Forms go to all Member School Districts; nominations cannot be made from the floor; election takes place at the June meeting. Directors may be removed with cause as defined in Appendix I by affirmative vote of a majority of the Members or Directors then in office. Failure to attend three (3) consecutive Board meetings constitutes a resignation unless an excused absence is requested in writing to the Board President within thirty (30) days.

ARTICLE VII - BOARD OF DIRECTORS. Special meetings may be called by the President or any two Directors, and Section 4 Notice is redlined to delete references to fax and U.S. mail as outdated modes of communication. A majority of the Board is a quorum. Directors receive no stated salaries, though a fixed sum and expenses of attendance may be allowed by resolution, and Board proceedings are confidential absent advance authorization. New Section 10 requires the Board to create and maintain Board Operating Procedures used in conjunction with the bylaws, the rationale noting the Board recently adopted such procedures defining roles, responsibilities and timelines.

ARTICLE VIII - OFFICERS. The Board elects from its own membership a President, Vice-President, Secretary and Treasurer. Section 2, Term of Office, carries the "Ther" to "The" correction and provides for removal with cause by affirmative vote of a majority of the Directors. The President is Chief Executive Officer and presides at Directors’ meetings; the Vice-President acts in the President’s absence. The Secretary records all votes and minutes and gives notice of meetings; the amendment allows the Office of Secretary to be divided annually at Board discretion into Corresponding Secretary and Recording Secretary, citing a Board of 7-9 directors and additional leadership opportunities. The Treasurer has custody of funds and securities and reports to the President and Directors. Officers may be required to furnish bonds at Association cost.

ARTICLE IX - COMMITTEES. Quorum is twenty-five (25%) percent of appointed representatives, each present representative having one vote, with alternates counting only when the primary representative is absent. Section 3 moves the annual chair election to the first committee meeting after July 1st, replacing January 31st, with written notice not less than seven (7) calendar days before the vote; the rationale is that the Operating Year is July 1 - June 30. Section 4 makes the Government Relations Committee a standing committee receiving information on legislative matters to share with Member School Districts, meeting at least 6 times per year, with district representatives appointed at annual organizational meetings, a Chairperson elected at the first committee meeting after January 31st, one (1) vote per district in attendance, and the OCSBA Vice President assuming Vice Chair duties absent an elected Vice Chair; Legislative Priorities are reviewed annually for Board approval. Section 5 makes the Resolutions and Bylaws Committee a standing committee meeting at least once per year, with members appointed annually by the OCSBA President rather than the Board of Directors and the Government Relations Committee Chairperson serving as a member. Member School District voting windows are at least forty (40) calendar days, and resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) Member School Districts become the official position of the Association.

ARTICLE X - DISSOLUTION. Assets are distributed as provided in Article VIII of the Articles of Incorporation, and no part of net earnings may inure to any Member, Director or Officer, as prohibited by Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 as amended, the Michigan General Sales Tax Act or the Michigan Use Tax Act.

ARTICLE XI - FIDUCIARY AND FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITIES. Expenditures may not exceed the approved annual budget. Board of Directors approval and signatures of both the President and Treasurer are required for any expenditure exceeding $2,500; expenditures up to $2,500 must be approved by either the Board President or the Treasurer, with the Vice-President approving if either is absent or disabled. The Treasurer distributes reports quarterly or on request, presents a budget for the upcoming fiscal year (July 1 to June 30) not later than the June Board of Directors meeting, and end-of-year revenue and expense reports no later than August 30th; the approved budget and annual report are presented at the first fall Member Meeting. Agreed-upon procedures are performed annually on the financial records, with an external audit only if required by law or a third party, and the Board may enter an Administrative and Financial Services Agreement with Oakland Schools, monitored by the Treasurer.

ARTICLE XII - INDEMNIFICATION. Eleven sections indemnify directors and officers to the fullest extent authorized by the Michigan Nonprofit Association Act. Indemnification is approved by majority vote of a quorum of disinterested Directors, by a committee of not less than two (2) disinterested Directors, or by independent legal counsel in a written opinion; other sections cover advancement of expenses, partial indemnification, employees and agents, liability insurance and severability.

ARTICLE XIII - FISCAL YEAR, determined by the Board of Directors. ARTICLE XIV - CONFLICTS, requiring officers, directors, committee members and employees to avoid conflicts; Section 2, Dealing with the Association, carries the deletion of a duplicate phrase; Section 3 requires notice of any direct or indirect interest and abstention; Section 4 excludes a conflicted Board member from the quorum count, with the minutes reflecting the disclosure, abstention and quorum situation.

ARTICLE XV - MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS. Conveyances and contracts, the signing of checks, drafts, bills of exchange, acceptances and notes, and the contracting of loans are governed by Board resolution. Section 5, Method of Giving Notices, is amended so notice is given by electronic communication to a director’s or officer’s last known district-provided email address, deemed given at the time of communication, with the rationale that OCSBA does not physically mail communications. Remote participation by conference telephone or similar two-way communication equipment constitutes presence in person.

ARTICLE XVI - AMENDMENTS, RULES AND REGULATIONS. Amendments are by vote of the Member School Districts on a written ballot with at least a forty (40) day voting period, one vote per district; grammatical errors that do not change meaning or intent may be corrected by the Board of Directors without a membership vote. During a declared local, state or national emergency the Board may set aside rules and regulations regarding meetings, elections and the conduct of Association affairs.

APPENDIX 1 - Definition of Cause for Removing a Board Member or Officer, adopted by the OCSBA Board of Directors on September 16, 2020. It recites the three primary legal duties of a nonprofit board - duty of care, duty of loyalty and duty of obedience - and defines cause as acts of malfeasance, misfeasance or nonfeasance; willful failure to follow OCSBA bylaws; willful neglect of duties; failure to disclose a conflict of interest or using the Association for personal gain; using the OCSBA Board position or logo in a political endorsement; frequently missed Board or committee meetings; creating an unhealthy or dysfunctional boardroom; and ethical concerns such as discrimination, harassment or criminal behaviors. Removal should only be done when absolutely necessary.

2025_313_ocsba_resolutions_showing_chang.paragraph: Redlined compilation of the Oakland County School Boards Association's legislative resolutions, showing 2025 recommended amendments to previously adopted resolutions alongside continuing resolutions, with adoption and amendment dates and cross-references to MASB resolution numbers. Under OCSBA Bylaws Article IX, Section 5, resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) member school districts become the official position of the association as interpreted and pursued by its board of directors. Proposed amendments touch accountability and transparency, broadband, mental health, school aid, the School Finance Research Collaborative, school nutrition, teacher shortages and early childhood.
2025_313_ocsba_resolutions_showing_chang.page:
**Framework**
A tracked-changes compilation of OCSBA resolutions adopted by member school districts, with adoption and/or amendment dates noted for each. The adoption standard quoted from OCSBA Bylaws Article IX, Section 5 is that resolutions approved by at least nineteen (19) member school districts shall be the official position of the association as interpreted and pursued by its board of directors. Page footers read "Revised March, 2023."

**2025 recommended amendments to previously adopted resolutions**
- ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019] - support for transparency and accountability for all school aid funds, holding every school receiving public funding to the same standards including FOIA requests and the Open Meetings Act, covering local districts, ISDs, Public School Academies (charter schools), their authorizers and management companies, and colleges and universities. Cites MASB Resolution A 6.65 (c), (d), (f).
- BROADBAND ACCESS AND DEVICES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021] - broadband in any federal or state infrastructure plan; support for funding to expand affordable and reliable broadband; support for programs to purchase internet-capable devices and software; and new support for dedicated cybersecurity resources. Cites MASB Resolution A-10.30 - 2021 amendment.
- MENTAL HEALTH [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019] - increased mental health services and professionals in schools with at minimum annual inflation-adjusted state resources; help staff identify potential mental health issues; encourage MDE to develop a model policy. Cites MASB Resolutions G 9.01, G 9.05, G 9.50.
- SCHOOL AID [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019] - opposition to using School Aid Fund dollars for anything other than K-12 education; constitutional specification that the fund is only for Pre-K to 12th grade public education and opposition to private school vouchers or tax credit programs; additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students; protection of the fund and local revenues from state tax policy changes; and enactment of the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so districts can meet the June 30 budget deadline. Cites MASB Resolutions A 10.25 and subsections, A 10.05 and A 10.55.
- SCHOOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (SFRC) [Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 9/11/2021; 3/3/2023] - support for implementing SFRC recommendations while holding higher funded districts harmless; the recommended studies on capital costs, infrastructure and transportation are noted as completed. Cites MASB resolution G 11.01 and A-10.25.
- SCHOOL NUTRITION [OCSBA Adopted 3/3/2023] - codification of free universal meals.
- TEACHER SHORTAGES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021] - statewide initiatives to address shortages and retain teachers, including incentives and easing Michigan certification for out-of-state teachers. Cites MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority.
- UNIVERSAL PRESCHOOL / EARLY CHILDHOOD [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019] - new dollars for universal public preschool for all four year old children and support for mandatory kindergarten for all five-year-old children. Cites MASB Resolution A 6.15 (c).
- ALIGNED AGENDAS [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019] - support for the NSBA, MASB, Oakland County Superintendents Association (OCSA) and newly added COSSBA legislative agendas, with links to masb.org/resolutions.aspx, nsba.org/Advocacy and cossba.org/advocacy.

**Continuing resolutions**
EVIDENCE-BASED DECISION MAKING [9/24/2019, MASB G 11.01]; LAME DUCK [9/24/2019]; LOCAL CONTROL [9/24/2019, MASB A 10.10, A 10.55, A 12.70]; SCHOOL SAFETY [3/3/2023]; SPECIAL EDUCATION [9/24/2019] supporting full funding of IDEA, noting federal legislation initially promised 40 percent of the excess cost of educating students with disabilities; and UNFUNDED MANDATES [9/24/2019, MASB A 10.20] opposing state or federal legislation that increases district costs without full funding.
2025_313_ocsba_resolutions_showing_chang.verbose:
"OCSBA Resolutions Showing Changes" is the redlined compilation of the Oakland County School Boards Association's legislative resolutions circulated with the Troy School District Board of Education materials for May 20, 2025. It opens by stating that the resolutions have been adopted by member school districts, that adoption and/or amendment dates are noted for each, and quotes OCSBA Bylaws Article IX, Section 5, Resolution Adoption: resolutions that are approved by at least nineteen (19) member school districts shall be the official position of the association as interpreted and pursued by its board of directors. Page footers are marked "Revised March, 2023," with pagination reading 1 of 3 on the first page and 2 of 4, 3 of 4 and 4 of 4 thereafter.

2025 RECOMMENDED AMENDMENTS TO PREVIOUSLY ADOPTED RESOLUTIONS

ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA supports transparency and accountability for ALL school aid funds - community governed public school districts, charter schools, cyber schools, community colleges and public universities - holding every school that receives public funding to the same accountability and transparency standards, including FOIA requests and the Open Meetings Act. This includes local districts, ISDs, Public School Academies (also known as charter schools), their authorizers and management companies, as well as all colleges and universities. Cross-reference: MASB Resolution A 6.65 (c), (d), (f). Rationale: expanded to include FOIA requests, OMA and additional school entities.

BROADBAND ACCESS AND DEVICES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021]. Broadband should be included in any federal or state infrastructure plan; OCSBA supports additional federal and state funding opportunities to expand affordable and reliable broadband access; OCSBA supports federal and state programs for the purchase of internet capable devices and software; and OCSBA supports dedicated resources for cybersecurity. Cross-reference: MASB Resolution A-10.30 - 2021 amendment. Rationale: update "we support" to "OCSBA supports" in all resolutions, and cybersecurity is a growing issue needing dedicated funding and support.

MENTAL HEALTH [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA supports increased mental health services and professionals in schools and adequate state resources providing, at a minimum, annual inflation-adjusted state resources to allow schools to both educate and keep students and staff safe. Bullet provisions call for helping staff identify potential mental health issues for students and encouraging the Michigan Department of Education (MDE) to develop a model policy for staff regarding identifying mental health issues and appropriate staff response. Cross-references: MASB Resolutions G 9.01, G 9.05 and G 9.50. Rationale: districts need consistent, annual funding for mental health.

SCHOOL AID [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. The lettered provisions oppose using School Aid Fund dollars for any purpose other than K-12 education [MASB Resolution A 10.25]; specify that the School Aid Fund is only for Pre-K to 12th grade public education in Michigan's Constitution and oppose any attempts to create private school vouchers or tax credit programs [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (a) and A 10.05]; support additional funding for Special Education, At-Risk and ELL students [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (g) and (j); A 10.55]; protect the School Aid Fund and local revenues from state tax policy changes [MASB Resolutions A 10.25 (c); A 10.55]; and support enacting the annual School Aid Budget no later than June 1 so that school districts have factual information to meet their constitutional and statutory requirement to approve a budget by June 30 [MASB Resolution A 10.25 (h)]. Rationale: items A and D were duplicative, so D is moved to the first bullet.

SCHOOL FINANCE RESEARCH COLLABORATIVE (SFRC) [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; Amended 9/11/2021; 3/3/2023]. OCSBA supports implementation of the recommendations of the SFRC; the redline strikes the qualifier limiting support to the recommended additional studies on capital costs, infrastructure and transportation. While implementing the SFRC recommendations, higher funded districts must be held harmless. Cross-reference: MASB resolution G 11.01 and A-10.25 - 2021 amendment. Rationale: those recommended studies have been completed, so the association now supports all of the SFRC's recommendations.

SCHOOL NUTRITION [OCSBA Adopted 3/3/2023]. OCSBA supports the expansion of the Free and Reduced Meals program to include all children as was done during the pandemic, with the redline replacing that phrasing with codification of free universal meals.

TEACHER SHORTAGES [OCSBA Adopted 9/11/2021]. OCSBA supports statewide initiatives to address teacher shortages and retain teachers while maintaining quality teacher preparation programs. Initiatives might include, but should not be limited to, incentives to enter and complete a teaching college program, incentives for teachers to remain in the classroom, and easing the process to obtain Michigan certification for teachers certified in other states. Cross-reference: MASB 2021-2022 Legislative Priority. Rationale: replace "we" with OCSBA to be consistent across resolutions.

UNIVERSAL PRESCHOOL / EARLY CHILDHOOD [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. The heading is changed from Universal Preschool to Early Childhood. OCSBA supports additional new dollars to fund universal, public preschool for all four year old children, and OCSBA supports mandatory kindergarten for all five-year-old children [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019; MASB Resolution A 6.15 (c)]. Rationale: public preschool dollars should not be used for vouchers or private or parochial preschools, and support for mandatory kindergarten is added because kindergarten is currently not mandatory in the State of Michigan.

WHEN ALIGNED WITH OCSBA LEGISLATIVE PRIORITIES, OCSBA ALSO SUPPORTS [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. The National School Boards Association (NSBA) Legislative Agenda; the Michigan Association of School Boards (MASB) Legislative Agenda; the Oakland County Superintendents Association (OCSA) Legislative Agenda; and the Consortium of State School Board Associations (COSSBA) Legislative Agenda. Links provided: MASB Resolutions at https://www.masb.org/resolutions.aspx, NSBA Advocacy IDEA at https://www.nsba.org/Advocacy, and COSSBA Advocacy at https://www.cossba.org/advocacy. Rationale: adding COSSBA to the list of associations with whom OCSBA aligns, since MASB belongs to both NSBA and COSSBA.

CONTINUING RESOLUTIONS - previously adopted by the members, with adoption and/or amendment dates noted.

EVIDENCE-BASED DECISION MAKING [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA supports evidence-based education policy that will maximize opportunities for the highest achievement of each student. Cross-reference: MASB Resolution G 11.01.

LAME DUCK [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA supports lame duck parameters that will address introduction and accelerated passage of legislation after the November election.

LOCAL CONTROL [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. Support for local control of community-governed public schools with elected school boards. Cross-references: MASB Resolutions A 10.10, A 10.55 and A 12.70. The same page repeats the mental health bullets on helping staff identify potential mental health issues and encouraging MDE to develop a model policy.

SCHOOL SAFETY [OCSBA Adopted 3/3/2023]. OCSBA supports that there be adequate state resources to allow schools to both educate and keep students and staff safe.

SPECIAL EDUCATION [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA supports full funding of the federal Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), noting that although federal legislation initially promised to provide 40 percent of the excess cost to educate students with disabilities, appropriations have fallen short, leaving states and local school districts to make up the difference. Cross-references: MASB Resolution A 5.01 and NSBA Advocacy: IDEA.

UNFUNDED MANDATES [OCSBA Adopted 9/24/2019]. OCSBA opposes any state or federal legislation that results in increased costs for school districts without full funding, and encourages the Michigan Legislature to oppose any federal laws or programs that are not fully funded and thus cost the state valuable resources. Cross-reference: MASB Resolution A 10.20.

The recurring editorial themes across the redline are converting first-person "we support" phrasing to "OCSBA supports," eliminating duplicated language within the School Aid resolution, broadening accountability language to name FOIA and the Open Meetings Act, adding cybersecurity and mandatory kindergarten as new positions, and adding COSSBA to the list of allied associations.
